summary: Red-and-white cast-iron tower on Motion Island off Random Island, Trinity Bay, first lit 1895. The Cooper family kept it to 1952; the Coast Guard owns it now and the tower is closed.

lens.note: Sixth-order lens (LighthouseFriends, 1895), occulting then; the Coast Guard text gives a flashing light on acetylene from 1931; Rowlett says solar-powered lens

structures.note: 10.2 m on the Coast Guard list; 10.4 m in LighthouseFriends and the Coast Guard text; 10 m in Rowlett; 9.1 m in the 2012 NL Historic Trust report
Stood 3.7 m north of the tower; demolished (Rowlett)

staffing.note: Coast Guard text: unwatched from 1931. LighthouseFriends and the Digest: Cooper caretaker until 1952. Battery power in the 1960s.

access.note: Coast Guard property. Reachable only by helicopter or by boat in very calm weather. Grounds open and tower closed (LighthouseFriends); site and tower closed (Rowlett).

events.note: Site at Heart's Content selected; cast-iron tower delivered there
Tower and keeper's dwelling erected on Motion Island after an executive decree moved the tower
Light could not start until early 1895 because the optical apparatus was late
Thomas Cooper appointed by letter of 15 April 1895 from J.T. Neville, Superintendent of Lights
George Havlock Cooper succeeds his father after Thomas Cooper's death
Changed to acetylene (LighthouseFriends); the Coast Guard text says it became a flashing white light
Coast Guard text: the light became unwatched; LighthouseFriends and the Digest keep a Cooper caretaker to 1952
Fanny Cooper dies at the lighthouse in July 1932; George Cooper retires the same year (LighthouseFriends)
Last Cooper caretaker resigns; the Digest says automation took over
Converted to battery power during the 1960s
Tower classified a Recognized Federal Heritage Building
Tower restored (Rowlett); refurbished in the late 1980s

keepers.name: Thomas Cooper
keepers.note: First keeper. LighthouseFriends names him Thomas Cooper and, in its letter sentence, Thomas H. Cooper; the Digest and the Coast Guard text give Thomas Henry Cooper; the society's copy of the 1895 contract is titled Henry Thomas Cooper. LighthouseFriends' roster ends him in 1904, but its text and the Digest give 1905. Second wife Roxana Stowe.

keepers.name: George Havlock Cooper
keepers.note: Son of Thomas Cooper by his first marriage. LighthouseFriends' roster ends him in 1931; its text says he retired in 1932. Wife Fanny Stowe, sister of Roxana.

keepers.name: Thomas Henry Cooper
keepers.note: Caretaker, son of George Cooper and named for his grandfather; the Coast Guard text calls the last full-time keeper Thomas Cooper, who resigned in 1952.

keepers.name: John Watton
keepers.note: Caretaker through the 1960s, when the light became battery powered. Named only in his public role.

corrections.why: The Coast Guard List of Lights gives 48 05 41.1 N, 053 32 43.1 W (48.09475, -53.54531), and LighthouseFriends gives 48.09475, -53.545306. The OSM point is about 0.0003 degrees north and 0.002 degrees east of the Coast Guard position.
The record's 'built 1895' is the first-lit year. The tower and dwelling were erected in 1894 and the light first shown in early 1895 (LighthouseFriends; Coast Guard text; 2012 report p. 40).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The first keeper appears as Thomas Cooper (LighthouseFriends roster and text), Thomas H. Cooper (LighthouseFriends' letter sentence), Thomas Henry Cooper (Digest, Coast Guard text) and Henry Thomas Cooper (contract title on the society's page). His grandson was also Thomas Henry, and the two are easily confused. The story keeps both names apart.
LighthouseFriends' roster ends Thomas Cooper in 1904, but its text and the Digest say he died in 1905. The story uses 1905.

The Coast Guard text says the light was unwatched from 1931 and the last full-time keeper resigned in 1952. LighthouseFriends and the Digest keep a Cooper as caretaker until 1952. The story reports both.
10.4 m (LighthouseFriends, Coast Guard text, Wikipedia lead), 10.2 m (Coast Guard list), 10 m (Rowlett), 9.1 m (2012 report). The story gives the old and current figures without choosing.

Coast Guard list: Fl W 5s, range 5 nm. Coast Guard text (earlier): flashing white, range 11 miles. Rowlett: red flash every 3 s. The Wikipedia lead gives Fl W 3s and 7 nmi, which is not cited. The Coast Guard list is taken as current.
LighthouseFriends says grounds open and tower closed; Rowlett says site and tower closed. Both agree the station is reached only by helicopter or boat.

notes_for_editor: Keeper names disagree across sources (see resolved_conflicts); the Cooper relationships are taken from LighthouseFriends and the Digest, which agree on the family. The 1931 unwatched date (Coast Guard text) and the caretaker to 1952 (LighthouseFriends, Digest) are both reported. The Digest article and the Coast Guard text are reprints on the Southwest Arm Historical Society site: the originals were not read. Not reached: the Newfoundland Journal of the House of Assembly for 1893 to 1895 (Heart's Content and Random Head contract), the 1895 contract itself (linked from the society page, not fetched), the Coast Guard book Lighthouses of Newfoundland and Labrador (read only in reprint), and Newfoundland newspapers (the Evening Telegram). The Wikipedia article was read as a lead only and is not cited. John Watton is named only in his caretaker role. The Cooper family members named in the sources are deceased; no living relatives are named. The stormy Christmas memory is undated and is reported as memory only.
